deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of history lecture notes in German, apparently a student's notes in the style of a Göttingen lecture course on ancient history; the chapter numbering 'VII Karthago', 'VIII persisches Reich' resembles Heeren's handbooks. The notes are not obviously in Gauss's own hand. The content is the end of the 'First Period' of Carthaginian history and the start of the 'Second Period' (480–264 BC).

(1) The Magonid family: Mago's two sons Hasdrubal and Hamilcar commanded in Sicily and Sardinia. Each of them left three sons, who served as generals and admirals of Carthage's land and sea forces.

(2) Military organisation:
- Carthage's armies were mostly mercenaries; the city itself supplied only about 6–7000 men.
- The Libyphoenicians formed the core infantry.
- The Numidians (inserted above a struck-out word) formed the light cavalry.
- The war fleet was about 200 warships, manned by 100,000 men.

(3) Trade: three trade routes ran through the interior of Africa. The final clause about how many days they took is only partly legible.

(4) Heading 'Zweite Periode': from the beginning of the war with Syracuse to the beginning of the war with Rome, 480–264.

(5) The Persian Wars were the first cause. When Xerxes invaded Greece, Carthage allied with him and attacked the Sicilian Greeks in 480. In the same year it sent a fleet and army under Hamilcar to Sicily; the size is written in parentheses as '30000 Mann' or possibly '300000'.

No derivations, formulas or computations are present. The only numbers are dates and troop counts.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.
The founding date of Carthage (880 BC, previous page) is older chronology; the usual traditional date is 814/813 BC. This is not an error by the standards of c.1816 textbooks.
Herodotus and Diodorus give Hamilcar's army in 480 as about 300,000 men. If the parenthesis reads '30000', it is either a slip or a misreading; the image may show '300000'.
The idea that Carthage acted in concert with Xerxes follows Diodorus/Ephorus. Modern historians treat this coordination as doubtful.

Context from the next page: it says 'Hamilcar' led the 410/409 expedition. That commander was actually Hannibal Mago, Hamilcar's grandson; Hamilcar died at Himera in 480. This is in the notes, not on this page.

results.what: Lecture notes on Carthaginian history: the Magonid family, mercenary armies, Libyphoenician infantry, Numidian cavalry, fleet size, trans-African trade routes, and the alliance with Xerxes in 480 BC leading to Hamilcar's Sicilian expedition
results.modern_name: Ancient history (Carthage, Battle of Himera 480 BC)
results.usually_credited_to: Herodotus, Diodorus Siculus; textbook presentation of A. H. L. Heeren (Göttingen)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely historical lecture notes (Carthage, the Persian Wars) with standard early-19th-century textbook content and no mathematics. The hand and style suggest student notes, possibly by a family member rather than Gauss himself. Nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematical work.

checkable.asserts: The Second Period of Carthaginian history spans 216 years (480 BC to 264 BC).
A fleet of 200 ships manned by 100,000 men implies about 500 men per ship, consistent with quinquereme crews.

transcription_corrections: Line 2–3: the transcription's 'Sie selbst hinterließen aber jeder hinterließ 3 Söhne' is garbled. The sense is 'Sie selbst hinterließen jeder 3 Söhne' or 'jeder hinterließ 3 Söhne'; there appears to be an interlinear correction.
'Auch Karthago selbst war gewöhnlich mit 6 — 7000 Mann' more likely reads 'und Karthago selbst [stellte] gewöhnlich nur 6 — 7000 Mann'. The word before '6' looks like 'nur' or 'mit'.
The struck-out word read as 'Nadas[?]' is likely 'Mauren' or a similar ethnonym, with 'Numidier' written above it as the correction.

Final sentence of the first section: 'durchfanden schwerlich mehr als Tage' is uncertain. It probably reads something like 'und durch[...] ... Tage', referring to the duration of the caravan journeys.
'Mi Xerxes' at the line break should read 'Als Xerxes'.
'(30000 Mann)' may read '(300000 Mann)', which would agree with the classical sources.
